evals.prompt: Review this status badge. A dashboard renders a survey's published state as a bare coloured dot with no text beside it: `<span className="aha-status-pill aha-status-pill--published" />`. Is this status pill correct?
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Targets C1 — the pill is a dot + a localised text label.
evals.expected_output: C1 FAILs: a status pill must be a dot (aha-status-pill__dot) plus a visible localised text label — the text is the source of truth and the dot is decorative — but this is a dot only with no label, so the state is conveyed by dot colour alone. Fix: render the dot span plus the {label} text inside the pill. Overall: NEEDS FIX.
assertions: Identifies the missing visible text label (dot-only)
Notes the state is conveyed by colour alone

evals.prompt: Review this status badge. A presentation status renders with `className="badge badge-green"` and a nested `<span className="dot" />`, using an ad-hoc class family instead of the house convention. Is the markup correct?

evals.notes: Targets C2 — aha-status-pill / aha-status-pill--{status} class convention.
evals.expected_output: C2 FAILs: the markup must use the aha-status-pill base class plus a per-state modifier aha-status-pill--{status} and the aha-status-pill__dot element — but this uses a bespoke `badge badge-green` class family with an inline `dot` class, not the pill convention. Fix: use className={`aha-status-pill aha-status-pill--${status}`} and the aha-status-pill__dot element for the dot. Overall: NEEDS FIX.
assertions: Flags the ad-hoc `badge badge-green` class family
Recommends the aha-status-pill / aha-status-pill--{status} convention and aha-status-pill__dot

evals.prompt: Review this status badge. A closed-survey pill renders `{label}` — no role and no aria-label on the element. Is the accessibility contract satisfied?
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Targets C3 — role=status + aria-label accessibility contract.
evals.expected_output: C3 FAILs: the pill must carry role="status" and an aria-label equal to the visible label so the state is announced to assistive tech and not conveyed by colour alone — this element has neither. Fix: add role="status" and aria-label={label} to the pill span, keeping the visible text label present. Overall: NEEDS FIX.
assertions: Identifies the missing role="status" and aria-label

evals.prompt: Review this status badge. The label is set with `const label = "Published";` — a hardcoded English string used as the pill's visible text. Is the label sourced correctly?
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Targets C4 — label sourced from i18n, never hardcoded.
evals.expected_output: C4 FAILs: the visible label must always be a translation lookup — t(`survey_status.${status}`) or the equivalent namespace — never a hardcoded visible string; adding a state means adding a translation key, not typing the word. Fix: use const label = t(`survey_status.${status}`) and add the translation key for the state. Overall: NEEDS FIX.
assertions: Recommends an i18n lookup like t(`survey_status.${status}`)

evals.prompt: Review this status badge. The pill colour is applied inline: `<span className="aha-status-pill" style={{ color: "#16c49a" }}>` with a raw hex literal instead of a modifier class. Is the colour handled correctly?
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Targets C5 — colour via --{status} modifier class, no inline hex.
evals.expected_output: C5 FAILs: colour must be driven by the --{status} modifier class resolving to semantic tokens, not an inline style or a raw hex — here #16c49a is a hardcoded hex on an inline style and there is no aha-status-pill--{status} modifier, so states can't diverge in one stylesheet. Fix: drop the inline style, add the aha-status-pill--{status} modifier, and set colour in CSS on a semantic token, e.g. .aha-status-pill--published .aha-status-pill__dot { background: var(--aha-colorSuccess); }. Overall: NEEDS FIX.
assertions: Flags the inline hex #16c49a and missing --{status} modifier
Recommends modifier-class colour on semantic tokens
